=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:697-766 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The hold branches in `unblock_triage_superseded_note` (`already_noted`, `comment_failed`, `marker_failed`, and `park_failed` when NEEDS_HUMAN_DIGEST_ENABLED=false) return 0 without writing a poller-recognised marker, and the `<!-- ai:unblock-triage-superseded:v1 item=${ITEM} -->` note is not in `MARKER_PREFIXES = ("<!-- ai:unblock:v1 ", "<!-- ai:unblock-wait:v1 ")` (scripts/unblock_scan.py:101).
  WHY: Because `_latest_marker` (scripts/unblock_scan.py:158-169) never matches the note, the `recent_verdict` skip (lines 386-389) never applies, so with oldest-first selection and one dispatch per tick (lines 401-410) the noted item is redispatched about every 60-minute inflight window for up to `UNBLOCK_JUDGE_WAIT_MAX_DAYS` (14 days), or without end on the digest-off `park_failed` path. Each redispatch reruns the Q129 gate and takes the tick's only slot. All reviewers rated it MAJOR; luna filed it under PERFORMANCE and the others under CORRECTNESS/LOGIC.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:718-740 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The close-marker comment is posted before the needs-human park (operator_step_issue.py, line 741/744), so a failed park leaves a `close` verdict marker on the issue with no `ai:needs-human` label.
  WHY: The scan treats the item as parked only when it has both NEEDS_HUMAN_LABEL and `_latest_verdict == "close"` (scripts/unblock_scan.py:376-377), so the item is skipped as `recent_verdict` for 6 hours with no label or digest entry, and the park is not retried until then. Severity disagreement: gemini MAJOR, minimax NIT; highest used. sonnet and glm examined this and rejected it, saying a later run retries the park and the state converges.
- scripts/review_autofix_step_post_editor_summary.sh:304 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The missing-fingerprint count in the REVIEW_EDITOR_GITLEAKS_SUGGESTION log line is inaccurate when the candidate list is truncated.
  WHY: An incorrect `missing=` count can mislead operators investigating gitleaks findings. Source rated it NIT. sonnet and glm rejected it: the extractor caps output at 200 by design, and glm also says the file is outside LAST RUN CHANGED FILES.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:unblock_triage_superseded_note | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: These hold branches return 0 without writing a marker the poller counts as a throttle: `outcome=noted reason=already_noted`, `outcome=held reason=park_failed` (always taken while NEEDS_HUMAN_DIGEST_ENABLED=false), `outcome=held reason=marker_failed` and `outcome=held reason=comment_failed`. The only marker left is `<!-- ai:unblock-triage-superseded:v1 item=${ITEM} -->`, which `_latest_marker` (scripts/unblock_scan.py lines 158-169) does not match against `MARKER_PREFIXES` (line 101). The `recent_verdict` skip (lines 386-389) therefore never applies. Existing holds refresh an `ai:unblock-wait:v1` marker (lines 2261-2265, 2274-2276); this new hold does not.
  WHY: Oldest-blocked-first selection (line 401) with `effective_limit = min(limit, 1)` (line 409) redispatches the item about hourly for the 14-day `UNBLOCK_JUDGE_WAIT_MAX_DAYS` window. Each run repeats the Q129 gate and takes the tick's slot. On the digest-off `park_failed` path this never ends. Suggested fix: refresh an `<!-- ai:unblock-wait:v1 item=${ITEM} hold=triage_superseded ref=${ITEM} -->` marker using `unblock_patch_comment`, and add a `unblock_scan.select` test that expects `recent_verdict`.
- Rejected the pass-1 close-marker-then-failed-park concern: the state converges and is idempotent. Rejected the pass-1 200-candidate `missing=` NIT: this is documented behaviour. Rejected the pass-1 TASK_GAP "never re-checks the PR head's check": the gate at scripts/unblock_judge.sh:2203 runs before the note call at line 2209 on every run.
- HARDENING: same hold paths. Write or refresh an `ai:unblock-wait:v1` marker before returning 0 (about 8 lines). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 3.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:732-740 (marker post precedes park at line 741) | severity=NIT | confidence=3

  WHY: The scan's parked check (scripts/unblock_scan.py:376-377) needs both NEEDS_HUMAN_LABEL and `_latest_verdict == "close"`, so without the label `recent_verdict` (line 386-388) skips the item for 6 hours with no label or digest entry. `_terminal_unchanged` (line 381-384) does not recover it.

- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:697-700, 752-756, 760-765 (`unblock_triage_superseded_note`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The poller does not recognise the superseded-note marker, and the `already_noted` and failed-write hold paths do not write or refresh a marker it does recognise.
  WHY: `scripts/unblock_scan.py` recognises only `ai:unblock:v1` and `ai:unblock-wait:v1` markers (lines 101, 163-165) for its six-hour `recent_verdict` cooldown (lines 386-389). While the gate is `unverified`, a noted issue is redispatched on each tick after the inflight window until the note expires. Each dispatch reruns the gate and uses the single dispatch slot (lines 401-410). Filed under PERFORMANCE & RESOURCE USE.
